writeup.headline: DocuSign rates Buy on a net-cash balance sheet, strong cash margins and a powerful price trend.
writeup.thesis: DocuSign's Buy rating and score of 69 rest mainly on a balance sheet score of 100 (net cash, no debt), a trend score of 82 and a quality score of 74. Quality reflects a 79.5% gross margin, a 35.6% FCF margin and a diluted share count down 8.5% year on year, offset partly by stock-based pay at 18.0% of revenue and a 12.0% operating margin. Valuation scores 67: in absolute terms P/FCF of 13.0x is low and the FCF yield is 2.7 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, while EV/EBIT of 36.9x is high. Against its own history it is cheap against its own history (EV/EBIT not comparable), with P/FCF cheaper than at 49 of the last 61 month-ends. Growth is the weakest factor at 52, with TTM revenue growth of 8.6%, though growth sped up by 0.7 pp from the previous quarter.
key_risks: Revenue growth is only high single digits (TTM revenue growth of 8.6%), which caps the growth score.
Stock-based compensation at 18.0% of revenue makes the 12.0% operating margin look thin next to free cash flow.
After a sharp run, the price is 53.7% above its 200-day average and 2.0% below its 52-week high, leaving room for a pullback.
EV/EBIT of 36.9x is high in absolute terms.
Analyst consensus remains Hold, and the IAM product push needs to keep delivering to support the raised FY27 guidance.
what_would_change: A drop of 5 points in the composite score would cut the rating to Hold, for example if the trend score fades as the shares cool off.
A rise of 11 points would reach Strong Buy, most plausibly through faster revenue growth lifting the growth score from 52.
Further IAM traction or another guidance raise could lift the news risk score of 55, while a guidance cut would push it down.
A fall in free cash flow margin would weaken both quality and valuation scores.
